paper_title: PyramidInfer Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM   Inference
caption: Comparison between PyramidInfer and full cache baseline with different batch sizes on the LLaMA 2-7B model with input length of 512+256.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates throughput as a function of batch size for two inference settings, comparing “PyramidInfer” to a “Full Cache” baseline on the LLaMA 2-7B model (input length noted as 512+256). The x-axis is labeled “Batch Size,” uses a linear scale, spans roughly from 0 to 64, and shows major tick labels at 0, 20, 40, and 60. The y-axis is labeled “Throughput (token/s),” uses a linear scale, spans roughly from 0 to about 2700 token/s, and has regularly spaced tick labels every 500 token/s (0, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500). The PyramidInfer series is drawn as a solid pink line with circular markers and increases across the batch sizes shown, starting near ~100 token/s at batch size 1, rising through ~350 (batch 4), ~680 (batch 8), ~1320 (batch 16), ~2050 (batch 32), and reaching about ~2650 token/s at batch size 64. The Full Cache series is drawn as a solid teal line with circular markers and rises from roughly ~130 token/s at batch size 1 to about ~340 (batch 4), ~630 (batch 8), ~990 (batch 16), and ~1230 token/s at batch size 32, then decreases to about ~950 token/s at batch size 64.
